metadata.title: Technology Capability Resilience
metadata.description: Hypothetical stressors test whether the proposed operating product remains useful when people, technology, evidence, or transaction timing changes.
metadata.naiveArchitecture: A principal produces a diligence report, runs informal CTO meetings, and rebuilds outcome and exit evidence when requested.
metadata.residualArchitecture: Company-owned decisions retain evidence from thesis through exit; explicit roles, suitable specialists, measurement contracts, scoped access, and reusable learning support adaptation.
metadata.note: Proposed scenarios only. No actual Vortex incident, probability, survival test, or implemented control is claimed.

stressors.name: The Technology Principal becomes unavailable
stressors.detection: Hypothetical: a departure, illness, or overlapping deals removes the principal from critical decisions.
stressors.attractor: The capability behaves like one person expertise; company relationships, context, and approvals stall.
stressors.businessReaction: Assign backup decision facilitators, retain company ownership, prioritize material commitments, and engage suitable contracted specialists.
stressors.residue: Accepted handoffs, role coverage, versioned decisions, and outcome-tested expert support make the product less dependent on one person.

impacts.effect: Make product leadership and decision support transferable without exposing confidential notes.
Maintain suitable backup specialist capacity and clear engagement scopes.
Retain accepted company owners and decision context.
Allow a consented transition to another coach.

stressors.name: AI changes a company technology value thesis
stressors.detection: Hypothetical: customer substitution, pricing pressure, or new AI economics contradicts the original defensibility claim.
stressors.attractor: The original thesis and roadmap continue to guide spending after their assumptions weaken.
stressors.businessReaction: Refresh customer evidence, revise the technology thesis, test a bounded AI or product response, and stop unsupported investment claims.
stressors.residue: Versioned assumptions and explicit stop/adapt/scale experiments remain useful across future market changes.

impacts.effect: Revisit moat and substitution assumptions with current customer evidence.
Test product, productivity, and disruption hypotheses with costs and quality.
Make revision of the value case an explicit management decision.

stressors.name: Portfolio measures stop being comparable
stressors.detection: Hypothetical: an acquisition, changed accounting basis, missing source export, or revised engineering metric breaks a cohort.
stressors.attractor: A portfolio dashboard continues ranking companies using incompatible ratios or incomplete data.
stressors.businessReaction: Quarantine affected imports, revise definitions and cohort membership, disclose unavailable comparisons, and use company-local evidence meanwhile.
stressors.residue: Versioned measurement contracts, compatibility checks, provenance, and explicit unavailable states improve every later comparison. Potential future reuse, once adopted: AI changes a company technology value thesis.

impacts.effect: Version denominators, periods, and source definitions.
Withhold comparisons that fail compatibility or disclosure rules.
Permit useful qualitative learning when quantitative comparison is unavailable.

stressors.name: Company evidence or coaching confidence is mishandled
stressors.detection: Hypothetical: a CTO discovers that private coaching, candidate information, or company evidence reached an unintended audience.
stressors.attractor: CTOs withhold context, peer learning collapses, and authorized reporting becomes harder.
stressors.businessReaction: Contain access, establish what was shared, follow the applicable company response process, revoke inappropriate grants, and agree a trust-rebuilding participation boundary.
stressors.residue: Separate note/claim permissions, named-audience approvals, expiry, audit trails, and minimum-data sharing protect future cooperation. Potential future reuse, once adopted: The Technology Principal becomes unavailable.

impacts.effect: Revoke and audit grants by company, purpose, and audience.
Keep private coaching content distinct from agreed escalation records.
Require explicit claim and audience approval.
Use approved aggregates and sanitized peer cases only.

stressors.name: Multiple acquisitions exceed technology integration capacity
stressors.detection: Hypothetical: several add-ons arrive while the company is still executing the original value plan.
stressors.attractor: Every platform is forced into one migration plan, leadership is overloaded, and customer continuity deteriorates.
stressors.businessReaction: Reassess retain/connect/consolidate choices, prioritize accepted business outcomes, phase commitments, and bring suitable specialist capacity.
stressors.residue: Explicit platform options, company responsibility maps, and staged acceptance make future integrations easier to adapt. Potential future reuse, once adopted: The Technology Principal becomes unavailable; Portfolio measures stop being comparable.

impacts.effect: Replan dependencies around company outcomes and continuity.
Preserve reversible platform options rather than mandate a stack.
Surface leadership and coordination capacity limits.
Use bounded expertise and an explicit capacity decision.

stressors.name: A buyer process starts earlier than expected
stressors.detection: Hypothetical: an unsolicited buyer or changed fund timetable creates an earlier technology diligence window.
stressors.attractor: The exit story must be reconstructed while company leaders are busy delivering the plan.
stressors.businessReaction: Use existing readiness evidence, separate substantiated claims from gaps, prioritize buyer-critical questions, and approve disclosures for the actual audience.
stressors.residue: Continuous readiness, reusable provenance, explicit gaps, and versioned approved answers remain valuable even if the transaction does not proceed. Potential future reuse, once adopted: Company evidence or coaching confidence is mishandled; Multiple acquisitions exceed technology integration capacity.

impacts.effect: Prioritize current evidence and material unresolved gaps.
Release only reviewed, audience-approved claims.
Reuse ownership history rather than invent a new narrative.
Coordinate a realistic response scope with company leadership.
